hindi: अचानक मरे हुए, तेल लगे हुए मृतक की परीक्षा करे।
english: He should examine one who has died suddenly, anointed with oil.
notes: āśu = quickly/suddenly, so āśu-mṛtaka = one dead suddenly. The text does not say who applied the oil or why. The subject of parīkṣeta (he) is not stated.

words.gloss: with the skin of the abdomen filled with wind
killed by breath obstructed through pressing

hindi: जिसका मूत्र और मल बाहर निकल गया हो, पेट की त्वचा वायु से भरी हो, पैर और हाथ सूजे हों, आँखें मुँदी हों और कण्ठ पर चिह्न हों, उसे दबाने से रुकी हुई साँस द्वारा मारा गया जाने।
english: One should know [him] to be killed by breath obstructed through pressing, if he has urine and faeces expelled, the skin of the abdomen filled with wind, swollen feet and hands, closed eyes, and marks on the throat.

text_flags.why: possible: nominative-looking mat-form among accusatives agreeing with hataṃ; accusative pāṇimantam expected
possible: ṭ for ḍ; the word for pressing is pīḍana

notes: vāta-pūrṇa-koṣṭha-tvakka: tvakka is read as 'skin' (tvac extended); alternative 'the abdomen and skin full of wind'. The English '[him]' is supplied. sa-vyañjana = with marks, signs (no cause stated). 'if he has' is the English rendering of the descriptive bahuvrīhis, which have no conditional word. Possible nominative pāṇimān could instead be read as 'he is one with swollen feet and hands' in apposition.

words.gloss: with arms and thighs drawn together

hindi: उसी को, जिसकी भुजाएँ और जाँघें सिकुड़ी हुई हों, फाँसी से मारा गया जाने।
english: That same one, with arms and thighs drawn together, one should know to be killed by hanging.
notes: tam eva refers back to the body described in unit 2. udbandha = hanging by a rope (ud-√bandh); hata is literally 'killed', so the text does not say whether the hanging was by himself or by another (see units 15-16).

words.gloss: with swollen hands, feet and belly

words.gram: m. acc. sg. pp. caus. ava-√ruh

hindi: जिसके हाथ, पैर और पेट सूजे हों, आँखें हट गई हों और नाभि ऊपर को उठी हो, उसे नीचे उतारा गया जाने।
english: One whose hands, feet and belly are swollen, whose eyes have gone away, whose navel is turned up, one should know [him] to be one who has been lowered.
notes: Doubtful words. apagata-akṣa 'eyes gone away' could mean eyes sunk in or protruding or displaced; kept literal. avaropita (ava-√ruh, causative, 'caused to descend') is obscure: it may mean one taken down, e.g. from a hanging, or one put down; no sense is chosen and the literal 'lowered' is given. There is no 'hata' here, so no cause of death is named.

words.gloss: with tongue clenched in the teeth

hindi: जिसका गुदा और आँखें जकड़ी हुई हों, जीभ दाँतों में दबी हो और पेट फूला हो, उसे जल से मारा गया जाने।
english: One with rigid anus and eyes, tongue clenched in the teeth, and bloated belly, one should know [him] to be killed by water.
notes: nistabdha-guda-akṣa is read as 'rigid anus and eyes' (both members qualified by nistabdha); alternative 'rigid anus-eyes' is unlikely. sandaṣṭa = pressed/bitten together.

hindi: जिसके रक्त से सिंचे अंग टूटे और फटे हों, उसे लकड़ियों या पत्थरों से मारा गया जाने।
english: One sprinkled with blood, with limbs broken and split, one should know [him] to be killed by sticks or stones.
notes: gātra = limb or body; here 'limbs'. The Hindi 'अंग' follows that.

hindi: जिसके अंग कुचले और फटे हों, उसे नीचे फेंका गया जाने।
english: One with limbs crushed and burst, one should know [him] to be one thrown down.
notes: avakṣipta = thrown down; the text gives no place or height. sphuṭita = burst, split open.

words.gloss: with dusky hands, feet, teeth and nails
with loose flesh, hair and skin

hindi: जिसके हाथ, पैर, दाँत और नाखून साँवले पड़ गए हों, मांस, रोम और चमड़ी ढीली हो और मुख झाग से लिपटा हो, उसे विष से मारा गया जाने।
english: One with dusky hands, feet, teeth and nails, loose flesh, hair and skin, and face smeared with froth, one should know [him] to be killed by poison.
notes: śyāva = dark brown, dusky; kept literal. carmāṇam is the bahuvrīhi form of carman (skin).

words.gloss: with a bite accompanied by blood
killed by a snake or insect

hindi: उसी को, जिसका दंश रक्त सहित हो, साँप या कीड़े से मारा गया जाने।
english: That same one, with a bite accompanied by blood, one should know to be killed by a snake or insect.
notes: tam eva refers back to unit 8. sarpa-kīṭa is read as a dvandva 'snake and insect', so 'snake or insect'. kīṭa = insect or worm; no species named.

words.gloss: with clothes and limbs flung about
one who has vomited excessively and purged

hindi: जिसके वस्त्र और अंग इधर-उधर फेंके हुए हों, जिसने अत्यधिक वमन और विरेचन किया हो, उसे मदन-योग से मारा गया जाने।
english: One with clothes and limbs flung about, who has vomited excessively and purged, one should know [him] to be killed by a madana compound.
notes: madana is kept as a name and no plant or effect is stated (glossary 14.1: yoga = compound here). ativanta-virikta: ati may qualify only vanta ('vomited excessively'), the pair read as one noun-phrase.

words.gloss: with throat hung up and cut

hindi: इनसे भिन्न किसी एक कारण से मारा गया, अथवा मारकर दण्ड के भय से जिसका कण्ठ लटका हुआ और कटा हुआ हो, उसे जाने।
english: One should know [him] as killed by some one cause other than these, or as one who, having killed, from fear of punishment has the throat hung up and cut.
notes: Syntax is loose: 'hatam' (killed by another cause) and the second member (one who killed and then, from fear of punishment, has throat udbaddha and nikṛtta) both depend on vidyāt. udbaddha = bound up/hung up, nikṛtta = cut; whether these mean self-hanging and self-cutting is not stated, so the literal sense is kept.

hindi: विष से मारे गए के भोजन के शेष भाग की पक्षियों के द्वारा परीक्षा करे।
english: He should examine the remainder of the food of one killed by poison by means of birds.
notes: vayas (n., plural vayobhiḥ) = bird. What the birds show is not stated.

hindi: हृदय से निकालकर अग्नि में डाले गए को, जो चिटचिट करता हुआ अथवा इन्द्रधनुष के रंग का हो, विष से युक्त जाने; अथवा जले हुए का हृदय न जला हुआ देखकर।
english: Having drawn [it] out from the heart and thrown [it] into the fire, [it being] crackling or rainbow-coloured, one should know [it] as joined with poison; or having seen the heart of the burnt one unburnt.
notes: The object drawn out from the heart is not named; the neuter singular endings suggest a piece (or the heart itself) is meant, but this is not stated. ciṭiciṭāyat is onomatopoeic (crackling, a denominative participle); indra-dhanus = Indra's bow, i.e. rainbow; the compound is read as 'crackling or rainbow-coloured' because of the following vā. The last clause has no verb: 'one should know [it as poison]' is implied by the first clause but not written, and is not supplied.

words.gloss: who has received too much harshness of speech and punishment
one who has designs on inheritance, livelihood or women

hindi: उसके परिचारक जनों को, जिन्होंने वाणी और दण्ड की कठोरता अत्यधिक पाई हो, खोजे; अथवा दुःख से पीड़ित या अन्य में आसक्त स्त्री-जन को; अथवा दाय, वृत्ति या स्त्री-जन पर दृष्टि रखने वाले बन्धु को।
english: He should seek out his attendants who have received too much harshness of speech and punishment, or women afflicted by distress or attached to another, or a kinsman with designs on inheritance, livelihood or women.
notes: Doubtful: atilabdha (ati-labdha) = 'obtained in excess', read as having received too much of the harshness; vāg-daṇḍa-pāruṣya is read as 'harshness of speech and of punishment' (vāk-pāruṣya + daṇḍa-pāruṣya, glossary 8.3 senses; the Book 3 senses 'verbal/physical injury' are possible). abhimantṛ is taken as 'one who has designs on / aims at'; alternative 'one who plots against'. dāya-vṛtti-strī-jana could also be read 'livelihood from inheritance, and women'.

hindi: उसी की मारे गए या फाँसी लटकाए गए के विषय में परीक्षा करे।
english: Just that he should examine in the case of one killed or hanged.
notes: tad eva refers to the search of unit 14. hata-udbaddha is read as a dvandva 'killed or hanged'; alternative 'killed and then hung up'. Hindi 'फाँसी लटकाए गए' renders udbaddha.

hindi: अथवा स्वयं फाँसी लगाए हुए का अनुचित अपमान खोजे।
english: Or, in the case of one hung by himself, he should seek out the improper ill-treatment.
notes: viprakāra = ill-treatment, wrong done to a person. 'svayam udbaddha' read as 'hung by himself' (self-hanged). The word order puts vā after udbaddhasya; it opens the alternative to unit 15.

hindi: अथवा सबके लिए स्त्री और दायभाग सम्बन्धी दोष, काम में स्पर्धा, प्रतिपक्षी से द्वेष, व्यापार-संस्थाओं का समवाय, अथवा विवाद के आधारों में से कोई एक, अथवा रोष का आधार है।
english: Or, for all [of them], [there is] a fault concerning women and inheritance, rivalry in work, hatred of a rival, a coming together of trade establishments, or any one of the grounds of litigation, or a ground of anger.
notes: The sentence has no verb; only a bare copula is supplied. Doubtful: paṇya-saṃsthā-samavāya (saṃsthā = establishment/standing; samavāya = coming together, association; sense could be a collision or association of trade interests); strī-dāyādya-doṣa could be 'fault regarding women and inheritance' or 'defect in inheritance by women'; sarveṣām vā is read 'for all [of them]', referring to the cases of unit 14-16. vivāda-pada = ground (title) of litigation.

hindi: हत्या रोष के कारण होती है।
english: The killing has anger as its cause.
notes: Hindi 'होती है' is the bare copula; the Sanskrit has the bahuvrīhi alone. roṣa = anger.

hindi: स्वयं नियुक्त किए गए पुरुषों द्वारा, अथवा चोरों द्वारा धन के निमित्त, अथवा समानता के कारण अन्य के शत्रुओं द्वारा मारे गए की हत्या की परीक्षा निकट के लोगों से करे।
english: He should examine from those near the killing of one killed by men commissioned personally, or by thieves for the purpose of wealth, or, from resemblance, by enemies of another.
notes: Doubtful: svayam-ādiṣṭa-puruṣa 'men commissioned personally' does not say by whom (the victim's enemy is likely, not stated); sādṛśyāt 'from resemblance' is kept literal (the victim being mistaken for another is a possible sense). āsannebhyaḥ is read as ablative 'from those near'; dative is also possible.

hindi: जिसने उसे बुलाया, जिसके साथ वह ठहरा या निकला, अथवा जो उसे हत्या-स्थान पर लाया, उससे पूछताछ करे।
english: He should question him by whom [the dead man] was called, with [whom he] stayed [or] set out, or [by whom he] was brought to the place of the killing.
notes: The dead man is the unstated subject of the participles; 'saha' is taken with yena (with whom). Whether prasthitaḥ is also 'with whom' is a reading; the alternative is 'set out' as a separate clause.

words.gloss: at the place of the killing

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. sam-√gūh

hindi: और जो उसके हत्या-स्थान के निकट घूमने वाले हों, उनसे एक-एक करके पूछे: “इसे यहाँ किसने लाया या मारा? हथियार के साथ, छिपाता हुआ या घबराया हुआ कौन आपके द्वारा देखा गया?”
english: And those who move about near his place of killing, he should ask one by one: “By whom was this man brought here, or killed? Who, armed, concealing, or agitated, was seen by you?”
notes: The closing iti is carried by the quotation marks only. In the quotation the objects of saṅgūhamāna are not stated (himself or something else). The question 'kena ... hato vā' is two verbal ideas under one 'by whom': brought here or killed. āsanna-cara is read 'moving near'.

hindi: वे जैसा कहें, वैसी पूछताछ करे।
english: As they would say, so he should question.
notes: Sense: follow up according to what they say; kept literal ('so he should question').

hindi: अनाथ के शरीर पर स्थित उपभोग की वस्तु और साज-सामान, वस्त्र, वेश अथवा आभूषण देखकर उनका व्यवहार करने वालों को
english: Having seen, of one without a protector, the article of use and equipment on the body, a garment, dress or ornament, those who deal in them
notes: The sentence continues in unit 24: tad-vyavahāriṇaḥ is read as the object of anuyuñjīta (24a), so the unit ends without its verb. anātha = without protector (helpless, unclaimed). upabhoga/paricchada kept as 'article of use' / 'equipment'.

hindi: उनसे संयोग, निवास, निवास का कारण, कर्म और व्यवहार के विषय में पूछताछ करे; तब खोज करे।
english: He should question [them about] the connection, residence, reason for the stay, and the work and the dealings; then he should carry out the search.
notes: Continues unit 23: the dealers are the first object of anuyuñjīta, the listed matters the second. saṃyogam is read as the dead man's connection (association) with persons; vyavahāra = dealings/business. 'karma' = work (glossary 5.3 sense).

words.gloss: under the sway of desire and anger

hindi: जो कोई काम और क्रोध के वश होकर रस्सी, शस्त्र या विष से भी स्वयं अपने को मार डाले, अथवा पाप से मोहित स्त्री।
english: Whoever, under the sway of desire and anger, would put himself to death himself, by rope, weapon or poison also, or a woman deluded by evil.
notes: ghātayet is causative ('cause to be killed') but with ātmānam means to kill oneself; svayam is 'himself'. 'vā api' is rendered 'or ... also'. The line has no main verb for the woman; units 26-27 continue about 'them' (tān).

hindi: रस्सी से राजमार्ग पर उन्हें चाण्डाल द्वारा घसीटवाए; उनके लिए श्मशान की विधि नहीं, और वैसे ही सम्बन्धियों की क्रियाएँ भी नहीं।
english: He should have them dragged away on the royal road with a rope by a caṇḍāla; for them there is no cremation-ground rite, nor likewise rites by relatives.
notes: tān refers to those who killed themselves (unit 25). caṇḍāla kept as the class name. sambandhi-kriyā could also be rites 'for' relatives; kept as 'rites by relatives'. 'tathā' is read as 'likewise' after the second na; the 'भी' in Hindi renders this.

words.gloss: the procedure of the rites that are duties for the deceased

hindi: उनका जो बन्धु मृतक के कर्तव्य की क्रियाओं की विधि करे, वह बाद में उनकी गति का अनुसरण करे, अथवा अपने जनों से छोड़ दिया जाता है।
english: But a kinsman of theirs who would perform the procedure of the rites that are duties for the deceased, he should afterwards follow their course, or is released from his own people.
notes: Doubtful: tad-gati 'their course' (fate/path) is kept literal; pramucyate 'is released' could mean he is cut off or abandoned by his kin, or freed from them; the sense is not settled here. paścāt could mean 'afterwards' or 'later'. preta = the deceased (glossary 5.3).

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. sam-ā-√car

words.gloss: from officiating at sacrifices and teaching

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. sam-ā-√car

hindi: वह एक वर्ष में पतित हो जाता है, पतित के साथ व्यवहार करता हुआ; यज्ञ कराने, पढ़ाने या योन-सम्बन्ध से; और उनके साथ व्यवहार करने वाला दूसरा भी।
english: He falls in a year, associating with a fallen one; [through] officiating at sacrifices, teaching, or a marriage connection; and another also, associating with them.
notes: Doubtful: yauna (pertaining to the womb) is read as 'marriage connection', alternative 'connection by birth'. patati/patita 'falls/fallen' is kept literal (the technical sense of loss of status is not added). The subject of patati is unstated ('he'); 'taiḥ' = with those (the fallen).
